main_body: Two stacked wooden crates; the larger one is at the upper left and a smaller one sits at the lower right. Each has a striped plank lid and a dark brown front with a diagonal brace.
top_band: Column x=15: rows 1-8 are a light tan plank lid (L 146/113 alternating stripes) under a 1-row mid-brown edge at row 0. Row 9 is a dark line (L 44), then the dark brown front runs from row 10.
evidence: In the scan, a light plank lid (rows 1-8, L 113-146) is separated from the dark front (rows 10-17, L 65) by a dark line at row 9, a step of about 80 L. That reads as a horizontal top above a vertical south face, on both crates. The lid is tall relative to the front, but it is clearly a surface and not a rim. The brace is painted flat, so the front is not recessed. The two crates share the same construction, so neither fails the contract.

style.evidence: The candidate has only 8 distinct colours and a median of 6 per tile, against 38-40 colours and 17-20 per tile in the references. Each material has few steps: the lid alternates two tans plus an edge tone, and the front is one brown plus a darker brace line. The outline is brown-tinted (only 12% neutral), so it is not a sticker look. The lid stripes give some texture, but the dark front is a nearly flat brown area with a single diagonal line and no grain or speckle. It looks clearly thinner than the stall and well references.
